title: Dominic and the Drop
premise: Lior Dunmore, a private security contractor who guards clients nobody trusts, is on duty the night a chartered flight's records vanish mid-air — along with everyone aboard, including the analyst he was secretly falling for. Pulled into the wreckage by an old handler from the network that trained him, Lior discovers the 'Drop': a protocol that erases people by deleting their paper trail before their bodies are found. To survive, he must burn the network that made him, choosing between loyalty to the men who raised him and the truth about what they did. In the end he trades his own records for the evidence that exposes them, becoming a ghost himself — free, nameless, and finally honest.
about_author: Casper Vane is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade inside the gray zone between corporations and governments before walking away. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to be untraceable.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A routine protection detail for a paranoid data-broker establishes Lior's polished lie: the fake name, the packed bag, the rules of staying invisible. He flirts with Mara Voss, a flight-risk analyst under adjacent contract, breaking his own first rule. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Flight 44
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Mara boards a red-eye to testify quietly; Lior watches her go against protocol. Mid-flight, every record of the aircraft evaporates — manifests, transponder logs, her booking. His calls to the client go dead. Emotional beat: dread arriving in the form of clean, bureaucratic silence.

chapters.title: What the Handler Wants
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with a cold flashback to training. His old handler, Sable, surfaces with an offer: help identify who ran the Drop and the network will let him live. Lior recognizes the recruitment script because he once wrote it for others. Emotional beat: the sick comfort of being wanted by the wrong people.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Alternating Lior and Mara (alive, held off-grid) POVs. Lior traces the deletion through a records broker; Mara works her captors, learning the Drop requires an insider signature. Their threads nearly touch via a shared contact. Emotional beat: two people refusing to be erased.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He finds the insider authorization — Sable's own countersignature — and realizes he's not the hunter but the fall guy being assembled. A friendly colleague tips off the network; Lior burns his safehouse and runs. Emotional beat: betrayal as clarity.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Debt
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. We see the network's logic through its true believer: the Drop protects order, and Lior was always the designated sacrifice. Sable genuinely loves Lior like a son, which makes the order easier to sign. Emotional beat: love weaponized into duty.

chapters.title: Mara's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She escapes during a transfer, carrying a memorized ledger of every person the Drop has erased. Wounded and hunted, she reaches Lior through the one channel neither side watches: a debt collector they both owe. Emotional beat: hope that costs blood.

chapters.title: Burning the Network
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Lior and Mara seed the ledger into dozens of hands so no single death can stop it, then walk into Sable's trap deliberately. Lior offers the only trade the network fears: his own total erasure in exchange for the evidence going public. Emotional beat: courage as self-destruction with purpose.

chapters.title: The Drop Runs Both Ways
chapters.summary: Climax, Lior's POV. In the room where names die, Lior triggers the protocol on the network's own leadership using Sable's countersignature, while Mara's ledger hits the open wire. Sable, given the choice to shoot or be deleted, hesitates — and the hesitation ends him. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, paid for in full.

chapters.title: No Records
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Mara's POV. Weeks later, a woman with no last name meets a man with no records at a border town bus stop. The network is gutted, the testimony delivered, and both of them are officially nobody. Lior finally unpacks the go-bag. Emotional beat: peace found in being unfindable together.
